transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-06
Time: 15:00 UTC (local attendees noted)
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CSM), Maya Chen (Atlas Meridian), Jonas Meyer (Atlas SRE), Priya Kapoor (Atlas VP Product), Ethan Ross (Atlas Finance)

Summary: quick sync to review current pilot health, discuss latency vs cost tradeoffs for model fidelity, and align on budget for a scaled canary in April. Customer wants clarity on unit economics and a short benchmark that shows expected per-1000-token cost at normal and peak loads. Also security/SSO brief was requested but deferred to a separate call.

Topics:
- Current usage & cost trends
- Reliability incidents last 30 days and mitigations
- Quantization and fidelity tradeoffs
- Pilot scale and rollout timeline
- Next steps: benchmarks, pricing spreadsheet, pilot kickoff

Action items (captured live): see action_items metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for carving this hour out. Um, quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya Chen: hey, Maya here — sorry for being late got pulled from another stand.
[00:09] Jonas Meyer: Jonas - SRE, all good.
[00:10] Priya Kapoor: Priya here.
[00:12] Ethan Ross: Ethan - finance.
[00:13] Carlos Rivera: Carlos from Redwood. Aisha on mute too.
[00:15] Aisha Khan: yeah hi, Aisha here.
[00:17] Lena Ortiz: cool, thanks. Agenda — we want to walk usage/costs, reliability items, then a quick technical on quantization/fidelity tradeoffs and finish with next steps. Maya, do you want to start with how the pilot is feeling on your side?
[00:30] Maya Chen: yeah sure. overall the chat flows look good, latency has been stable at low qps. um we did see two spikes last week - one around Wed where p95 went up to about 1.1s which is fine but then we had a control plane retry that added about 300ms to some sessions. nothing catastrophic yet. we're more worried about token burn — cost is creeping. we want to understand whether moving to a 4-bit quantized variant would save materially and what the accuracy hit is.
[00:58] Carlos Rivera: got it. we can run an apples-to-apples microbenchmark with your prompts — compare baseline fp16 on gpus vs int4 quantized variant on same hardware or a slightly smaller instance. that should give per-token cost and a measured quality delta.
[01:18] Jonas Meyer: also from infra side, we saw a KV-cache thrash event when sequence lengths jumped. was there any guidance on prefix caching?
[01:28] Aisha Khan: that's something we flagged in the pilot notes — Redwood's runtime does automatic prefix caching but if the request patterns vary the caching hit rate drops. Carlos, do you want to explain the short-term mitigations?
[01:40] Carlos Rivera: yeah, so two quick levers: short-term we can tune cache TTL and use request routing to pin a percentage of traffic to nodes with warmed caches. medium term, we can enable prefix-aware batching in the serving runtime which improves hit rate but needs a short config tweak. both low-risk.
[02:00] Priya Kapoor: how does that affect latency SLOs? we can't risk adding 200-300ms for tail requests.
[02:07] Carlos Rivera: tuning TTL generally helps tail; prefix-aware batching actually lowers p95 in many workloads since it reduces duplicate KV recompute. there is a small batch-induced micro-latency at the very low qps tail, but overall you should see p95 stable or improved. the micro-benchmarks will show numbers.
[02:28] Lena Ortiz: on cost side, Ethan, were you able to look at last month's invoice? anything surprising?
[02:35] Ethan Ross: yeah we reviewed it. the two things — token volume is up 38% month-over-month because some of the dev builds are sending long debugging prompts, and there's an embedded rerank job spiking at midday. we need a clean per-route breakdown.
[02:49] Maya Chen: we suspected dev telemetry noise. can Redwood provide a per-route token/latency/cost export for the last 30 days?
[02:56] Aisha Khan: we can, and we typically include token-level breakdowns per route per model. I'll attach the CSV after the call.
[03:04] Jonas Meyer: also, any suggestions for controlling developer spikes? we could set quotas but want graceful behavior.
[03:11] Carlos Rivera: policy engine — set soft quotas with informative 429 messages and a developer sandbox environment pinned to a cheaper model. you can also enable client-side sampling for heavy debug flows.
[03:22] Priya Kapoor: ok that helps. next, on fidelity — what's the expected delta for int4 compared with your validated reference?
[03:29] Carlos Rivera: depends a lot on prompt distribution. some tasks are very robust to quantization, some sensitive ones (financial numbers, extraction tasks) see measurable delta. typical end-to-end quality delta at int4 is in the 0.5-2% range on our evals for conversational tasks; for extraction it could be higher. we'll run your three prompt sets to get concrete numbers.
[03:48] Maya Chen: and between using int8 and int4, is int8 a safe middle ground?
[03:52] Carlos Rivera: yes, int8 often gives most of the cost savings with far less fidelity loss. you pay a bit more than int4 but often it's a better trade for business-critical outputs.
[04:03] Ethan Ross: from finance side, what's the ballpark per-1k-token cost we should expect after quantization?
[04:09] Carlos Rivera: rough example — baseline fp16 route we showed last month was about $0.80 per 1k tokens. int8 might bring that to $0.45-$0.55; int4 could be $0.28-$0.35, depending on instance packing and cache hit rate. we'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[04:29] Maya Chen: do those figures include prefix cache savings?
[04:33] Carlos Rivera: good point — no, that's pure per-token compute. with high prefix cache hit rates effective per-req cost can fall another 15-35% depending on reuse.
[04:44] Priya Kapoor: reliability incidents — can we get a quick review of what triggered the control plane retry?
[04:49] Aisha Khan: logged as a transient controller fail during a routing table update; it retried and the runtime fell back to an older route for about 25 seconds which led to some duplicate tokens for a subset of sessions. postmortem recommended a routing rollout guard.
[05:05] Jonas Meyer: what's the mitigation cadence? we need a permanent guard before canary.
[05:09] Carlos Rivera: we can add a rollout gate that prevents controller changes during high-traffic windows and a quick rollback policy. low friction.
[05:20] Lena Ortiz: all right — let's talk pilot timeline. our ask was April canary with about 5% of production traffic for two weeks. realistic?
[05:28] Maya Chen: yes, 5% for two weeks is what the product team wants to measure. must include both fidelity variants and the baseline.
[05:35] Carlos Rivera: we can support blue/green style canary with model variants and an automatic fallback to baseline on quality regressions. we'll instrument quality monitors tied to the prompt set you share.
[05:47] Priya Kapoor: what quality monitors do you recommend? we can't manually review all sessions.
[05:52] Carlos Rivera: use a combination: automatic semantic similarity checks (embedding distances), a small human review sample (1% of sessions), and precision/recall checks for extraction tasks. Redwood Optimize can run those and surface regressions.
[06:10] Ethan Ross: procurement — assuming pilot looks good, how much runway do we need to finalize budget?
[06:15] Lena Ortiz: typical enterprise lead time here is 3-5 weeks once finance signs off. Ethan, you mentioned procurement timelines?
[06:22] Ethan Ross: we'll need internal approval windows but I think end of March we can commit to a pilot budget; production commitment would be mid-late April depending on legal.
[06:30] Maya Chen: legal also asked for SOC2 attestation and KMS usage details — we deferred the deep dive, but can Redwood send the security pack?
[06:38] Aisha Khan: yes, we have a security docs bundle. I'll share SOC2, ISO artifacts, KMS integration notes, and a short FAQ for auditors.
[06:45] Jonas Meyer: please include log retention and access controls — we need proof of per-token audit logs and RBAC.
[06:50] Carlos Rivera: noted; we'll include the console screenshots and API examples for audit log export.
[06:56] Lena Ortiz: quick live ask — Maya, can you drop the three prompt sets by end of day Tuesday?
[07:02] Maya Chen: yes I'll share them by 2027-03-08 EOD.
[07:05] Lena Ortiz: great. Carlos, you'll run the micro-benchmarks once you have the prompts and return results?
[07:10] Carlos Rivera: yes, run both int8 and int4 comparisons plus a baseline. want to test a warmed cache scenario and a cold cache scenario. results by 2027-03-11.
[07:19] Priya Kapoor: and then Lena you'll send a tailored price workbook?
[07:22] Lena Ortiz: yep, I'll fold in the benchmark numbers and a modeled cost per 1k tokens under different cache hit assumptions and send by 2027-03-09.
[07:30] Ethan Ross: one more finance note — can we get an amortized cost for retried tokens/duplicate tokens from the control plane incident? we need to understand how to bill for retries during pilot.
[07:40] Carlos Rivera: we'll dig into the logs and compute retry token deltas and propose an adjustment clause for the pilot contract if the retry rate is above threshold.
[07:48] Maya Chen: sounds fair.
[07:50] Aisha Khan: I'll include a short blurb in the next email on how retries are handled in the billing system.
[07:56] Lena Ortiz: ok wrapping — quick recap of next steps: Redwood shares security pack (Aisha) and pricing workbook (Lena) by 2027-03-09; Atlas shares prompts by 2027-03-08; Carlos runs micro-benchmarks and sends results by 2027-03-11; Ethan confirms budget window by 2027-03-12 and we pencil in pilot kickoff week of 2027-04-04.
[08:20] Priya Kapoor: agreed. any blockers?
[08:23] Maya Chen: none immediate.
[08:25] Jonas Meyer: none.
[08:26] Ethan Ross: no.
[08:27] Lena Ortiz: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts and scheduling invites.
[08:31] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some proper nouns auto-transcribed (e.g., KV cache -> K V cache) and occasional speaker label drift; numbers were approximate when discussed (Lena/Carlos provided rough per-1k token estimates pending benchmark).

References mentioned: cost workbook (will be shared), security pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS notes), benchmark spreadsheet (SE deliverable).
